fingerprint.session: CachyOS/KDE Plasma 6 Wayland, RS3 NXT via XWayland
fingerprint._note: Regions are pixel offsets measured on this exact window size. At any other size they resolve elsewhere and fail silently - OCR returns nothing, or reads a neighbouring panel. ui_scale 1.75 is the logical-to-physical factor KWin reports (2194 logical vs 3840 pixels); `doctor` detects it independently and reports it.

window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. RS3 pins panels to edges at fixed size rather than scaling them, so this survives a window resize. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

metrics_xp._note: XP and XP/h number rows in the Metrics panel

chat_tail._note: most recent ~15 lines of All Chat; w trimmed to end of text so the 3D world does not bleed into OCR. dy=-36, not -57: at -57 the region boundary fell mid-line, so the newest message - the one rules care about most - was clipped to ~10px of its 17px height and OCR'd as garbage on every cycle. -36 is the largest offset that still excludes the chat input bar below it.

backpack._note: full backpack panel. grid is relative to the region's top-left; verified against a hand count of 24 occupied slots

rules.name: pack_nearly_full
rules._note: Advance warning: fires when the projected time-to-full drops under lead_seconds. Paired with pack_filling, which is the overflow backstop - this one says 'about to fill', that one says 'already full and idle'. Distinct sounds so they are told apart without looking. lead_seconds=15 against a measured mean transit of 23s and a fill rate of ~19 slots/min. cooldown=55 is just under the 73s mean cycle, so it fires at most once per bank trip. EXPECT roughly one alert per trip: that is the cost of advance warning at this cycle length - switch this rule off if it becomes noise again. log_occupancy=false because pack_filling owns the log; two writers would double every transition and corrupt `watcher.py stats`.

rules.name: pack_filling
rules.alert_body: Pack has been full for {stuck:.0f}s - fishing has stopped. Bank to resume.
rules._note: Overflow mode, not lead-time. Measured over 12 cycles with `watcher.py stats`: mean cycle 73s, mean peak 27.0/28. A predictive warning therefore fired once per bank trip - ~50 alerts an hour - while the stats showed the trips were already being banked correctly without it. Overflow only fires once the pack has been full for overflow_seconds, which is the point where catches are genuinely being lost. Set mode to 'lead' with lead_seconds to go back to predictive warning; that suits a slow grind (mining, woodcutting) where the walk to the bank is long relative to the fill.

rules.name: xp_stalled
rules._threshold_note: measured: static floor 0.001, XP tick 1.3-4.0. No mask - the Metrics panel is opaque, and a brightness mask only added antialiasing flicker.
rules._disabled_note: Superseded by fishing_stopped, which detects the same event from chat in 30s instead of 60s. Two rules firing for one spot move is just double beeping. Metrics XP is also the weaker signal: it stalls identically whether the spot moved, the client was minimised, or the panel was closed. Re-enable for a grind with no per-action chat message, where XP is the only evidence of progress.

rules.name: impling
rules.pattern: a creature is discovered while skilling|an impling (has )?appear
rules.alert_body: An impling spawned nearby - catch it before it despawns.
rules._note: Implings spawn silently and despawn; the message is easy to miss mid-grind. Rare enough to deserve its own sound - message-highlight is distinct from the warning tones used by pack_filling and xp_stalled, so it is recognisable without looking. Long timeout because the impling despawns: the popup should still be on screen when you glance over.

rules.name: fishing_stopped
rules.pattern: you catch a|you cast out your line|you attempt to catch
rules.suppress_pattern: can'?t carry any more|do not have any space in your inventory|not have any space
rules.alert_body: No catch for {quiet:.0f}s - the fishing spot has moved.
rules._note: Fires when catch messages stop arriving, which is the only evidence that a fishing spot has depleted and moved - RS3 does not announce it. Measured over 166 real catch intervals from the occupancy log: median 3.7s, p95 10.0s, p99 19.7s, max 21.3s. stop_seconds=30 clears that max by ~9s so normal variance cannot false-fire. The pattern also matches the cast/attempt lines so a slow first catch after recasting does not count as stopped. suppress_pattern is essential: a full pack halts fishing outright, so catch messages stop on EVERY bank trip. Without it this rule fires once per cycle - the same ~50/hour noise the inventory rule was retuned to avoid. VERIFIED against live Menaphos fishing (Sept 2026): all three alternatives match real chat - 'You cast out your line...', 'You attempt to catch a fish.', and 'You catch a beltfish/desert sole/catfish'. Measured catch gaps there were median 2s, max 3s - faster than the 3.7s median this was originally tuned against, so stop_seconds=30 keeps ~27s of margin and needs no change.

rules.name: urn_full
rules.alert_body: The fishing urn is nearly full - replace it to keep earning urn XP.
rules._note: A fishing urn stops collecting once full, so every catch after that is wasted urn XP until it is teleported. RS3 announces one-quarter / half / three-quarters / full; only the last two are worth interrupting for, which is why the pattern skips the first two. Observed wording: 'Your decorated fishing urn is three-quarters full'.

rules.name: urns_carried
rules._prime_note: Requires a reading with urns actually present before any shortage can alert. Without this the rule fired on a cold start: `_armed` defaults to true, so launching the watcher with an empty or banked backpack announced 'No urns remain' within confirm_seconds - six times in the logged history, all of them the 'out' state, with no fishing under way at all. The alert claims the urns ran OUT, so it should have to watch them run out. A genuine drain still alerts normally: once any 'ok' count is seen the rule is primed for the rest of the session.
rules.out_message: No urns left - urn XP is being lost on every catch. Restock.
rules._note: Counts urns actually carried, by icon colour. urn_supply watches the BANK coming up short across trips; this watches the pack right now, which is the 'I only have one left' case - the two are independent. Colour beats OCR here: reading the stack digits was measured flickering between 6, 13 and 1 on an unchanging stack, while blueness (mean B - mean R of the icon's bright pixels) separates cleanly - urns +104/+105, coins -174, fish -10..-62. Verified 2/2, 1/1 and 0/0 against real captures at every threshold from 20 to 80. confirm_seconds=8 because a bank or loot interface hides slots and would otherwise read as a false 'out'; a real drain persists, an overlay clears in a frame or two. warn_below=1 fires at exactly one urn left.
rules.out_alert_body: No urns left - urn XP is being lost on every catch. Restock.

rules.name: out_of_supplies
rules.pattern: you (have )?(ran|run) out of|you do not have enough|not enough (space|room)
rules.alert_body: Out of supplies - check bait and free space.
rules._note: Deliberately does NOT match 'Item could not be found in the quantity required'. That fires on every bank preset load, because the preset requests more bait than is actually carried - it is normal, not a fault. Matching it made the rule fire once per bank trip.

rules.name: level_up
rules._note: Fires on any skill level-up, combat skills included - Attack, Strength, Defence and Constitution all produce the same 'advanced a <Skill> level' line, so no separate combat rule is needed. The last alternative additionally catches the overall combat level changing ('You are now a combat level 138'), which is a distinct and rarer event: per the wiki, combat level derives from Attack, Strength/Ranged/Magic/Necromancy, Defence and Constitution, so a single Attack level may or may not raise it. Deliberately does NOT require the leading 'Congratulations', because RS3 splits some notices across lines and the level line alone must still match - the same two-line shape that made the stun rule match the wrong line. Checked against 10 phrasings plus OCR-garbled forms, and against near misses that must stay silent: 'You need level 75 Attack to wield this', 'Total level: 1544', and 'Your combat level is high enough'. UNVERIFIED against this account's live chat - confirm the wording on the next level-up and tighten if it differs.

_notification_note: Rules use urgency 'normal' with an explicit timeout_ms so KDE auto-dismisses them. Setting urgency to 'critical' makes KDE keep the popup until it is closed by hand and ignore timeout_ms - only do that for an alert you must not miss.
